title: ICE Agent Castro Federally Indicted on 6 Counts of False Statements; First Federal Charge Against Surge-Era ICE Officer
excerpt: A federal grand jury indicted ICE agent Christian Castro on six counts of making materially false statements to investigators about the January 14 Minneapolis shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, marking the first federal criminal charge by the Trump administration against an ICE officer for conduct during its nationwide immigration surge operations.
content:
On September 3–4, 2026, federal prosecutors unsealed a grand jury indictment charging ICE agent Christian Castro, 52, with six counts of making materially false statements to FBI investigators about the shooting of Venezuelan immigrant Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis on January 14, 2026, in north Minneapolis during Operation Metro Surge.

  • The indictment alleges Castro falsely claimed he was violently attacked with a broom and snow shovel and that his confrontation with a suspect lasted approximately three minutes — prosecutors say the interaction lasted roughly eleven seconds and no such assault occurred.
  • The charges mark the first federal case by the Trump administration against an ICE officer for conduct during its nationwide immigration surge enforcement operations.
  • Castro pleaded not guilty in Texas federal court and was released on a $75,000 unsecured bond with a GPS ankle monitor. He is scheduled for a Minnesota federal court appearance on September 18.
  • Castro also faces separate state felony charges in Minnesota: four counts of second-degree assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime.

The case involved significant internal DOJ conflict. Federal prosecutors in Minnesota had initially prepared to charge Castro with the more serious offense of deprivation of rights under color of law — akin to charges used against officers who killed George Floyd. DOJ leadership in Washington blocked those charges over the lead prosecutor's "strongest possible" objections.
